Committee of Supply debate on Ministry of Home Affairs Head P

Committee of Supply (Head P of the Estimates)27 February 2026 budget-2885

A Committee of Supply debate on Head P of the Estimates for the Ministry of Home Affairs, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' speeches and ministerial responses.

The debate covers Home Team policies on terrorism, cyberattacks, drugs, scams, rehabilitation, fire safety and road safety. The transcript states specific changes including extending Fire Certificate validity from one year to three years from 1 April 2026, planning to bring RHA measures into force by end-2026, and amending FICA to allow anticipatory directions against online communications.

MINDEF budget debate and withdrawn $100 amendment

Committee of Supply debate on Head J of the Estimates27 February 2026 budget-2884

A Committee of Supply debate on Head J (Ministry of Defence) of the Estimates, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved and later withdrew an amendment to reduce the allocation by $100.

The Minister said MINDEF/SAF will build a suite of conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities, acquire three Gulfstream G550 maritime surveillance aircraft, and scale unmanned platforms paired with manned platforms. He also said MINDEF will take care of NSmen and NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance where budget space allows, regularly review NSF allowances, and do more for HOME awards, NS credits and tax incentives where possible. The debate also covered cross-domain cooperation with other agencies and new international partnerships on cyber, information warfare and critical underwater infrastructure.

Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs budget

Committee of Supply27 February 2026 budget-2883

A Committee of Supply debate on Head N, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved to reduce the total sum by $100 and Members questioned ministers on foreign policy.

The record says foreign policy shapes Singapore's food security, energy resilience, jobs and safety abroad, and that supply-chain disruption affects jobs, cost of living and business confidence. It also records MFA consular assistance for Singaporeans overseas, including during emergencies.

Open questions from this debate (12)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • How many Singaporeans are currently seconded to the ASEAN Secretariat, and how many more will be seconded ahead of Singapore's 2027 chairmanship?
  • What benchmarks does MFA use to assess whether its engagement sessions build durable public understanding?
  • Will Singapore accept the US invitation to join the Board of Peace, or participate as an observer?
  • What is the specific timeline for opening the resident embassy in Mexico?
  • What concrete outcomes or milestones can be expected under Singapore's ASEAN chairmanship for the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement?
  • What is Singapore's forward plan and contribution to alleviating the humanitarian crisis in Gaza?
  • How will MFA work with MINDEF and other security agencies to strengthen diplomatic, economic and defence resilience?
  • Will MFA upgrade its technology directorate to ambassador level or adopt a national technology strategy?
  • How is MFA working with the Ministry of Trade and Industry to reduce exposure to geopolitical chokepoints?
  • How will MFA embed geopolitical literacy in the school curriculum with the Ministry of Education?
  • How is MFA prioritising partnerships with middle powers and emerging regions?
  • How is MFA strengthening engagement at the sub-national level with Malaysian states and Indonesian provinces?

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 71 (complete)
  • Briefs on this page: 3 (114 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 98% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
